events.title: Register Now for 26.2 in ’26
events.description:
Hike (or Run or Walk) 26.2 miles in Van Cortlandt Park in 2026!

The Challenge:

Hike 26.2 miles in Van Cortlandt Park anytime during 2026, post on social media (@vcpalliance) from the park to spread the word, and wear your 26.2 in ‘26 Finisher’s Pin with pride once you attain your goal (because you earned it!).

VCPA will provide you with route options within Van Cortlandt Park, the third largest park in NYC, but you pick your method (hike, run, stroll, skip) and you pick when (as long as you complete it all by December 31, 2026). Van Cortlandt Park, located in the Northwest Bronx, has over 20 miles of trails of various levels of difficulty. If any of the suggested trails are too strenuous, you can substitute as you like. The specific trails do not matter as much as hitting the goal of 26.2 miles.

Registration:

Register now to receive the list of 9 different trails you can hike and some start-up swag! More details below.

Registration closes October 15, 2026 but the sooner you register, the more perks you will receive, and the more time you will have to meet the challenge.

Cost/Proceeds:

For only $52 per adult ($26 for those under 18), you can participate, receive swag, and make a difference in Van Cortlandt Park. You also gain access to exclusive hikes in the park, led by fabulous (and knowledgeable) VCPA staff. All proceeds support Van Cortlandt Park Alliance’s environmental education, internship and community stewardship programs.

The Swag:

Every participant gets a VCPA bag, VCPA die-cut sticker, VCP map, and invitations to exclusive 26.2 in ‘26 guided hikes (optional but will count towards your 26.2 miles). After you complete your hikes, you will receive an exclusive 26.2 in ‘26 Finishers Pin and bragging rights! Pins will be mailed starting in Fall of 2026.

Register Now.

events.title: Trail Work Thursdays
events.description:
Help Maintain the Trails that Keep the Park Connected

Be part of the community crew that cares for Van Cortlandt Park’s trails! Whether you’re a seasoned trailblazer or trying trail work for the first time, your effort makes a real difference in keeping these paths accessible and safe.

📍 Meeting Details:

Location: Location: VCPA Learning Garden

Time: 9:00 AM arrival — we begin hiking to the site promptly at 9:15 AM

🛠️ What We’ll Be Doing:

• Clearing debris, branches, and overgrowth

• Closing “desire lines” (unofficial paths) to protect habitats

• Ensuring trail safety and erosion control

• Learning best practices in trail care and stewardship

🧰 What to Bring:

• Comfortable, weather-appropriate clothing

• Sturdy closed-toe shoes (required)

• Reusable water bottle and snacks

• We’ll provide gloves, tools, and guidance!

🌟 Why Join Us?

• Protect the trails that make Van Cortlandt Park accessible to all

• Learn trail maintenance skills in a beautiful urban forest

• Enjoy the satisfaction of meaningful, hands-on stewardship

• Meet others who care about nature and want to give back

RSVP Now.

Groups of 6 or more must email stewardship@vancortlandt.org to coordinate their own event.

events.title: Birding with NYC Bird Alliance
events.description:
Van Cortlandt Park Alliance and NYC Bird Alliance invite you to join us during 4 weekend mornings of birding in the park this fall.

Explore Van Cortlandt Park’s ecologically diverse grounds and celebrate a long tradition of birding in the park. We will look for various species of resident and migratory birds and discuss a wide range of avian topics. Each walk will be led by a NYC Bird Alliance guide.

Advance registration is required. You must register separately for each date you would like to attend.

Birding sessions meet at 9am on the following dates:

  • Sunday, September 20
  • Sunday, October 4
  • Sunday, October 25
  • Saturday, November 21

Note: We do not provide binoculars and suggest that attendees bring their own.

Want us to continue birding programs in the future? Please make a donation during checkout. All donations made will be used to continue birding programs.

As space is limited, if you are not able to attend please let us know ASAP so we can fill in your spot by emailing info@vancortlandt.org.

These birding events are generously supported by NYC Bird Alliance.

Photo by Jack Rothman

events.title: Van Cortlandt Nature Group
events.description:
Take a slow walk in the park and learn about local flora and fauna with naturalist Debbi Dolan.

Signs of fall are all around us. Fall migrant warblers have been coming through, and the raptors are crossing the skies of Van Cortlandt Park. Soon the winter residents will be coming in like the white throated sparrow and northern shovelers. Hummingbirds have been filling up on jewelweed nectar in preparation for their southern migration. The Tibbetts Meadow is looking glorious with asters, goldenrod and staghorn sumac that are providing sustenance for the hungry migrant species and our resident birds.

Animals are beginning to fatten up ahead of winter, and since farmers had recently cleaned out their fields under the Harvest Moon, hunters could easily see the deer and other animals that had come out to root through the remaining scraps.

Meeting at the Van Cortlandt Nature Center.

RSVP Now.

events.title: Wetland Wednesdays
events.description:
Hands-on restoration in the park’s wetlands and floodplain. What we do shifts with the season — check the individual date before you sign up.

By season: water chestnut removal on Van Cortlandt Lake in summer; phragmites control and planting native willows and shrubs in fall.

When: Wednesdays, 9:00 AM – 12:00 PM

Where: Van Cortlandt Golf House — meet outside the VCPA offices next to the bathrooms

Bring: clothes that can get wet and muddy, water bottle, sunscreen. Long sleeves and boots for the phragmites dates.

Tools, gloves and training provided. No experience needed.

Ages 15+ welcome (minors need waiver).

RSVP Now.

Groups of 6+ email noel@vancortlandt.org to schedule separate event for a modest fee.

events.title: Youth Run Farm Stand
events.description:
We are very excited to bring our Youth Run Farmstand featuring fresh local produce at affordable prices back!

Wednesdays 2-7pm
from July 8 to October 28
Train Park (Gale Place and Orloff Avenue)

We accept WIC, FMNP Checks, EBT, Snap, Fresh Connect Checks, Cash and Credit/Debit.

events.title: Caribeando at the Farmstand
events.description:
This workshop provides an excellent opportunity to learn and practice Caribbean musical and dance traditions rooted in African heritage.

Learn and practice Caribbean musical and dance traditions including Bomba, Plena, Guaracha, Cha-cha-cha, Merengue, and more.
All ages, abilities, and skill levels are welcome to explore the basic rhythms, steps, call-and-response interactions, and shared community joy.
Caribeando is sponsored by The NYC Green Fund Grassroots Grant Program.

Get up and dance to earn a $2 Health Buck that can be used at VCPA’s Youth Run Farmstand on Wednesdays through 10/28 from 2pm to 7pm.

Event held at the VCPA Youth Run Farm Stand located at Gale Place and Orloff Avenue.

RSVP Now.

events.title: Super Seedlings – Family Gardening Fun
events.description:
This October, you’re invited to the VCPA Learning Garden for FREE family garden fun!

Super Seedlings is a FREE, drop-in gardening program for kids ages 2-7 and their caregivers.

Each session will have a fun seasonal theme to explore, crafts, plants to water, veggies to harvest, soil to dig into, and more!

Come once, twice, or all three weeks for some playing and planting! We hope to see you there!

📅 Dates:

Saturday, October 10th*

Saturday, October 17th

Saturday, October 24th 🎃

🕐 Time: 10 AM – 12 PM

📍 Location: VCPA Learning Garden

Enter through the park entrance off of Mosholu Avenue and Broadway – our garden is past the Northwest Playground and next to the Riverdale Stables.

*Please note: 10/10 is the day of the Manhattan College Invitational Cross Country Race in VCP. Parking will be extremely difficult. We recommend taking public transporation to the garden that day.

RSVP Suggested.

For more information, contact gardening@vancortlandt.org.
